title: Formspec Posture Declaration
description: Per-deployment posture declaration consumed by WOS admission (ADR-0090 D8). Declares signature policy, jurisdictional posture, and custody requirements for a deployment.

x-lm.intent: Version pin for posture declaration compatibility.

url.description: Canonical URL where this posture declaration is published.

x-lm.intent: Deployment URL for this posture — workflows reference this.

version.description: SemVer of this posture declaration document.

x-lm.intent: Semantic version for pinning posture declarations.

allowedMethods.description: Subset of registered signature-method URIs admitted by this deployment.

x-lm.intent: If a signature method is not in this list, admission emits SignatureAdmissionFailed { reason: method_unsupported }.

minimumPrimitiveVerification.description: Minimum primitive verification status required for admission. verified: cryptographic check must pass. deferredPendingHelper: helper-not-bundled is acceptable.

x-lm.intent: Floor for admission — if adapter returns deferredPendingHelper but posture requires verified, admission fails.

receiptSigningRequired.description: When true, VerificationReceipt MUST carry receiptBytes (signed receipt). When false, unsigned receipts are accepted.

x-lm.intent: If true and receipt lacks receiptBytes, admission emits SignatureAdmissionFailed { reason: posture_floor_unmet }.

allowedSigningIntents.description: Allowlist of signing-intent URIs admitted by this deployment, including deployment-local URIs. Supersedes workflow-level deploymentLocalSigningIntents (PLN-0384 sunset).

x-lm.intent: Deployment-scoped signing-intent allowlist — replaces workflow-level bridge field.

mode.description: Revocation checking policy. strict: must verify and fail on revocation. soft: check but warn. none: skip revocation checks.

notarialRequirements.description: Notarial requirements when framework requires notary involvement.

requiresTrellisExport.description: When true, Trellis export is required for signature custody proof.

requiresUca.description: When true, User-Content Attestation is required for byte-level corroboration.

requiresTimestamping.description: When true, external timestamping authority receipt is required.

allowedModules.description: Deployment allowlist of modules admitted by this posture. Admission rule per ADR 0150 §4.4: every field present on the posture entry MUST equal the corresponding field on the document's `modules[]` entry; fields absent on the posture entry admit any value on the document side. A posture entry `{id, version}` admits any document entry with the same id+version regardless of publisher/lockHash; a posture entry `{id, version, lockHash}` requires byte-identical lockHash on the document side. This is the seam that closes hostile-substitution risk: bare URN allowlists admit any module reusing the URN, but `{id, version, lockHash}` pins what the bytes must look like.

x-lm.intent: Field-equality admission — every present posture field must equal the corresponding document field; absent fields admit any value. Pinning lockHash closes hostile-substitution risk.

allowedActors.description: Deployment allowlist of authoring-identity URNs admitted by this posture. Per ADR 0150 §5.4: actor admission is binary (allowed / not), not provenance-pinned the way modules are — a flat URN list, not a ModuleRef shape. A deployment refuses authoring acts from actors whose URN isn't in the allowlist.

x-lm.intent: Binary actor admission — URN present in list admits the act; URN absent refuses it. URN pattern enforces `urn:formspec:actor:` prefix; product nuance (kind, channel) rides URN-encoded in the id segment.

propertyNames.description: Extension key grammar. (a) every key is an `x-` identifier in lower-kebab; (b) the `x-formspec-` sub-namespace is RESERVED and closed to the two hooks ADR 0150 §5.4 minted — a near-miss like `x-formspec-actorscope` is a typo that would otherwise ride the open seam through unvalidated and unenforced, so it is a schema error, not a passthrough key.

extensions.description: Extension namespace for this posture declaration — the sole open seam on an otherwise closed document (ADR 0056). Every key MUST be an `x-`-prefixed lower-kebab identifier. The `x-formspec-` sub-namespace is reserved and closed to `x-formspec-actor-scope` (constrained here per ADR 0152 §4) and `x-formspec-class-scope` (shape-open, presence-constrained per ADR 0152 §8 — see its own entry). Every other `x-` key rides through unvalidated.

x-lm.intent: Open seam on a closed schema, with a CLOSED x-formspec- sub-namespace: a misspelled reserved key is a schema error, not an unvalidated passthrough. Unknown non-formspec x- keys are admitted unconstrained and are NOT a licence to fail open at evaluation.

ClassScope.title: Per-widget-class write scope — RESERVED, deferred to ADR 0152 pass 2
ClassScope.description: Per ADR 0152 §8: zero consumers, so the inner shape stays UNCONSTRAINED — pass 2 owns it, and pinning it now would freeze a shape no consumer has asked for. Only presence is constrained. `null` is the JSON idiom for explicit no-config and is VALID — identical to absence, the same idiom `x-formspec-actor-scope` uses (§5.1), and the branch-open gate already reads it as not-configured. `{}` is invalid: `minProperties` bites on the object branch only, and `{}` is neither an enforceable declaration nor an absence — studio-core's presence test reads it as not-configured, so an author who meant to declare something would be silently skipped. Any non-empty payload validates here and is refused at branch-open with `class-scope-deferred` until pass 2 lands. Deployments meaning 'no class scope' omit the key or write `null`.

x-lm.intent: Presence-only constraint over an object-or-null type. `null` ≡ absent (explicit no-config, matching actor-scope). `{}` is a schema error — it silently reads as not-configured downstream. Any non-empty object validates here and is refused at branch-open until pass 2.

ActorScope.title: Actor write authority over authored vocabularies
ActorScope.description: Per ADR 0152 §4.1: binds closed vocabulary handles to actor selectors. `null` is the JSON idiom for explicit no-config — treated as absent, leaving binary `allowedActors[]` admission only (§5.1). Every other non-conforming payload (including `{}`, which is declared intent whose version cannot be read) is `posture-config-invalid`: a declaration that cannot be enforced admits nobody. Declaring this extension obliges the deployment to run strict posture handling — the non-strict fail-open is incompatible with it (§5.3). The posture document is host-supplied and author-immutable within a session; no kernel op writes it.

x-lm.intent: Fail-closed by construction. `null` degrades to binary admission; anything else malformed rejects the whole declaration rather than degrading. Never treat an unparseable actor scope as absent.

$actorScope.description: Version pin for the actor-scope extension. An unknown value makes the whole declaration unenforceable, so it fails closed rather than degrading to binary admission (ADR 0152 §5.1).

x-lm.intent: Unknown version rejects the declaration — it does NOT fall back to binary allowedActors[] admission.

protects.description: One entry per protected vocabulary handle. A handle absent from this list is governed by binary `allowedActors[]` admission only, unchanged. `[]` is a valid no-op declaration; the key being absent entirely is a malformed v1 document — the distinction is deliberate (ADR 0152 §5.1). Duplicate `vocabulary` values are `posture-config-invalid` with no merge semantics; JSON Schema cannot express that uniqueness constraint, so evaluation enforces it.

x-lm.intent: Empty array = valid no-op; absent key = malformed. Duplicate-handle rejection is NOT schema-expressible — evaluation owns it.

ProtectedVocabulary.title: One vocabulary handle bound to the actors permitted to write it
ProtectedVocabulary.description: Per ADR 0152 §4.1. Authority rules say WHO may write; graph rules (e.g. `THEME-ROUTE-CLASS`) say what is valid once written. This entry MUST NOT absorb graph validation, context conditions, or read/disclosure authority (§4.3).

values.description: OPTIONAL value-grain rule: vocabulary value → its own selector (e.g. any admitted human may set non-theming route classes, only named actors may set `intake`). Composition is **REPLACE**, pinned by ADR 0152 §4.1: a `values[<value>]` selector REPLACES the entry's `writableBy` for that value — it is not intersected with it. Absent values fall back to `writableBy`, and evaluation consults exactly one selector per write. Replace admits narrowing AND deliberate divergence: a freeze entry (`writableBy: {}`) plus per-value overrides expresses default-deny-with-allowlist, which intersection cannot. A value selector that admits an actor the entry selector excludes is declared authority, not an accident. Legal only on vocabulary-kind handles; on an operation handle it is `posture-config-invalid` (ADR 0152 §4.2/§5.1). A key outside the handle's closed vocabulary is `posture-config-invalid`.

x-lm.intent: REPLACE, not intersect: a values[v] selector fully supplants writableBy for value v, so it can widen as well as narrow. Widening is declared authority, not a bug.

allOf.title: Value grain is legal only on the vocabulary-kind handle `surface.routeClass` (ADR 0152 §4.2)

propertyNames.description: Closed `Route.routeClass` vocabulary (surface.schema.json). Only `intake` admits tenant theming — see `ROUTE_CLASS_THEME_AUTHORITY`.

VocabularyHandle.description: Vocabulary-handle registry v1 (ADR 0152 §4.2), CLOSED. `surface.routeClass` is a vocabulary-kind handle (value grain legal) protecting `Route.routeClass` writes. `theme.declaration` and `theme.assignment` are operation-kind handles (no `values`) protecting Theme declaration and theme token/ref assignment respectively. `theme.declaration` is a pending-op row: `declareTheme` does not exist yet, so declaring it binds the obligation but enforces nothing until that op lands. Growing this list is an amendment to ADR 0152, not a schema edit; an evaluator meeting an unknown handle MUST fail closed.

x-lm.intent: Closed registry — unknown handle rejects the whole declaration. `theme.declaration` currently has no landing op, so it declares intent without enforcement.

ActorSelector.title: Actor selector — union match over kind and id
ActorSelector.description: Per ADR 0152 §4.1: an actor writes iff its `kind` appears in `kinds` OR its id appears in `ids`. No prefix or pattern matching. An empty selector — `{}`, or every listed array empty — is a valid FREEZE: no actor writes that vocabulary. Locking a vocabulary outright is a legitimate deployment stance, not a malformation (§5.1). Unknown keys are malformed.

x-lm.intent: `{}` is a deliberate freeze, not a no-op and not an error. Union semantics across kinds/ids — never intersection.

kinds.description: Subset of the terminal-closed `AuthorActor.kind` vocabulary. Closed by the kernel actor model, not extensible here.

ids.description: Exact authoring identities, matched byte-for-byte — no prefix or pattern matching. Authors SHOULD use the `allowedActors[]` URN space (`urn:formspec:actor:…`); the URN shape is deliberately NOT pinned here so schema validity and studio-core's `parseSelector` return the same verdict for the same document. An id outside the actor URN space is dead config, not a schema error. `\S` IS pinned, because `parseSelector` rejects whitespace-only ids (`id.trim() === ''`) — without it the two layers would disagree on `" "` (ADR 0152 §4.1).
